title: Signal
description: The canonical, source-agnostic observation object (PR-002). An observation, not an interpretation — carries no pattern or review data. Every source adapter (rss/github/sec/nasa/arxiv) normalizes into exactly this shape. Pattern scoring and review lifecycle live on the separate Candidate object (candidate.schema.json) once a Signal is normalized. See docs/signal-lifecycle.md for the full chain and the Signal.status vs Candidate.review_state split. NOTE: `required` describes the complete, persisted Signal returned by a read, not a normalizer's insert payload — the three `readOnly: true` fields below (signal_id, hash, created_at) are populated by Postgres itself and must be omitted when constructing an insert.

signal_id.description: Stable unique identifier for this signal. DB-assigned default (gen_random_uuid()) — do not set on insert.

source.description: Specific origin within source_type, e.g. a named RSS feed, a tracked GitHub repo, a CIK/ticker, a NASA feed name.

source_type.description: Adapter family that produced this signal, matching sources/*: rss | github | sec | nasa | arxiv.

headline.description: Short human-readable title of the observed content.

summary.description: Optional longer excerpt/description, if the source provides one.

url.description: Canonical link to the source content. Part of the dedup hash input — see docs/signal-lifecycle.md.

published_at.description: When the source published the underlying content.

hash.description: SHA-256(SHA-256(source_type) || SHA-256(source) || SHA-256(url)) — the outer digest of the three inner 32-byte digests concatenated as raw bytes, hex-encoded (see docs/signal-lifecycle.md §2 for why a plain delimited join was rejected). The dedup key. Deliberately excludes headline/published_at so a corrected headline or republish timestamp doesn't mint a new signal. A Postgres GENERATED column — omit on insert; the database rejects any caller-supplied value outright, it does not merely ignore it.

normalizer_version.description: Version of the specific source normalizer that produced this record. Lets the classifier be re-run against historical signals without losing original ingestion history.

schema_version.description: Version of this canonical Signal schema itself, distinct from normalizer_version. Lets historical rows self-declare which schema revision they were written under.

status.description: Signal-level status only: has this raw signal been normalized into a Candidate yet? Immutable once NORMALIZED. All subsequent review/promotion lifecycle lives on Candidate.review_state, not here — see docs/signal-lifecycle.md.

created_at.description: Row creation timestamp. DB-assigned default (now()) — do not set on insert.
